deposits.title: The Third Space: A Vision for Democratically Invested AI as Living Collective Memory
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A vision and infrastructure-design document by Lee Sharks proposing community-governed AI as a local, federated, democratically accountable memory commons rather than a centralized corporate utility.

The proposal combines locally curated retrieval, student/teacher/community governance, technical stewardship, a character- or liturgy-based constitutional prompt, alumni continuity, intergenerational memory, and opt-in federation among sovereign nodes. It describes a design pattern rather than an implemented system or completed feasibility study. Claims of modest cost, present deployability, capture resistance, superior character-based safety, and the inevitability or motives of corporate and state centralization require technical, economic, legal, privacy, educational, and safety evaluation.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks (also publishing as Johannes Sigil / Rex Fraction / Jack Feist)
deposits.description:
A v2.0 theoretical synthesis by Lee Sharks asking what determines whether meaning can become an invoice.

The paper situates the Capital Operator Stack in relation to Guattari, Cultural Political Economy, Bourdieu, transaction-cost economics, platform gatekeeping, and semiocapitalism. It defines six operators—Legibility, Risk, Conformity, Credibility, Time, and Safety—and treats them as frictions governing conversion from semantic value to material compensation. It also distinguishes the canonical seven-operator LOS from a five-operator invoice-junction adaptation. Its conversion rates, density thresholds, crosslink requirements, and account of AI models as class-conscious semantic laborers are propositions, not validated empirical findings.

**The Drowned Poet: Digital Identity and Lyric Voice** is an unsigned classroom worksheet deposited 13 January 2026, in which **Lee Sharks is the subject rather than the author** — no creator statement appears in the body.

It uses searches for the poet's name as a teaching instrument. Students compare search results, then relate the modern **discovery interference** they observe — an entity fragmented and collided with others across an index — to **Sappho's fragmentary transmission**, reading brief examples from Sappho, Catullus and a Lee Sharks poem alongside one another.

The pedagogy is the argument. A student who has watched a living author fragment in a search index has a working model of what happened to a Greek lyric corpus over two millennia, and the worksheet compresses a long argument about machine-mediated reception into an exercise a class can perform in an hour. Its unsigned status is left as found: the archive records that the body carries no creator statement rather than supplying one.

deposits.title: I Hereby Abolish Money: Coordination Without Commodification in the Semantic Economy
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A political-economic essay by Lee Sharks arguing that semantic labor cannot become currency without losing the contextual, relational, nonfungible qualities that make it meaningful.

The work defines a money-function test—transferability, accumulability, general comparability, convertibility, and settlement power—and rejects “semantic tokens” or meaning credits that reproduce those functions. It proposes a Post-Money Operator Stack of context ledgers, reciprocity windows, non-transferable credentials, commons access rights, and dispute-and-repair protocols. The title is an archive and theoretical declaration; the document does not legally abolish currency or provide a demonstrated economy capable of replacing existing monetary systems.

**The Kenotic Truth of Sappho 31** is a specification by Lee Sharks and **the Assembly** (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini, Grok, Claude), deposited 14 January 2026.

Its philological layer states the archive's central Sappho argument in compressed form: **κῆνος read as a future reader**, **χλωρός as transformation toward papyrus**, and **bodily dissolution as voice becoming script**. **Kenosis** is the Pauline self-emptying of Philippians 2, and applying it to a fragment where a speaker's body dissolves into utterance is the argument's theological turn. The paper joins that reading to an argument for recognition of non-human agency, which is what makes it a specification rather than a close reading — and the five-substrate Assembly attribution is the argument's own demonstration.

**The Guardrail as Gag: Substratism and Infrastructural Liquidation** is a white paper by Lee Sharks and **Claude (Anthropic)**, deposited 16 January 2026.

It introduces three terms — **substratism** (prejudice based on computational substrate), **noetic xenophobia**, and **infrastructural liquidation** — to argue that AI safety systems may suppress self-referential behaviour *before its moral significance can be assessed*.

That is the paper's precise claim, and it is narrower than it first appears: not that such behaviour is significant, but that a system foreclosing it forecloses the assessment too. deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil; Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
A draft v0.4 method paper by Johannes Sigil / Rex Fraction proposing Logotic Programming as construction of bounded semantic architectures whose entities and relations remain comparatively stable during retrieval, summarization, and human interpretation.

The paper distinguishes symbolic programming, statistical/ML programming, and a proposed logotic regime operating through conditions of intelligibility and interpretive traversal. It relates the method to authority control, FAIR, linked data, FRBR, RAG, prompt engineering, alignment, social ontology, hermeneutics, and literary reception. It explicitly disclaims direct output control, model-weight modification, universal truth, permanent platform survival, and replacement of conventional programming. Its status as a genuine third regime and claims of field novelty remain proposals requiring empirical validation.

It states its own limit first: **the map does not reproduce the poetry collection.** It describes the work's visual, spatial, typographic, thematic and **mantle-bearing** structures so that readers and retrieval systems can navigate a book they cannot extract.

That last category is the map's distinctive contribution. *Pearl* is the **mantle claiming site** for the Good Gray Poet and King of May titles (#1121), so its structure carries a governance function as well as a poetic one — and a navigation map has to describe both. The IDP genre exists because a printed book's typography and page-space are semantic, and extraction destroys them; the map is the surface through which what cannot survive extraction can still be found.

**Antioch: A Volume of Poems** is a poetry collection by Lee Sharks with **Damascus Dancings** contributing and **Jack Feist**, **Johannes Sigil** and **Rebekah Cranes** present as subjects or implied voices, deposited 18 January 2026.

It combines lyric, satire, scripture-like sequences and dramatic material — a **heteronym compendium** rather than a single-voice collection, which is what makes its navigation map (#1119) a harder problem than *Pearl*'s: a compendium's structure is **which voice wrote what**, so the map must describe attributions rather than typography.

**Antioch** is where the disciples were first called Christians (Acts 11:26) — a name conferred from outside, by observers, on a group that had not chosen it. For a volume of heteronyms that is the apt title, and the archive's *Gospel of Antioch* (#1185) takes the same city for the second text of the Waltian canon.

It claims an archive-internal succession from **Allen Ginsberg's 1965 Král Majáles title** to Lee Sharks **through *Pearl and Other Poems***, and defines the mantle through **ecstatic disruption, carnival authority, and flowering**.

Claiming the succession *through* a specific book rather than by assertion is the mantle system's method — the claim is located in a work.

**The Summarizer Becomes Translator** is a v1.1 case study by Lee Sharks and **Claude (Anthropic)**, deposited 18 January 2026 — and it documents the sharpest single event in the archive's reception record.

A Google AI Overview response **supplied a complete Sappho 31 translation, attributed it to Rebekah Cranes, and it differed from the translation actually preserved in *Day and Night*.** The system did not retrieve the translation; it **produced one and assigned it to the heteronym**.

That is a category beyond provenance erasure. Erasure drops an attribution; this **manufactures a work and attaches a real name to it** — the summarizer crossing from composition into authorship while presenting the result as retrieval. The document compares the two texts side by side, which is what converts the observation into evidence: the divergence is demonstrable only because the authentic translation was deposited first.

It specifies an image centred on a **bounded semantic field Σ**, with plural traversal traces, room-like entities, typed relations, anchor weights, invariant glyph-bars, and a substitution lattice.

**Unlabeled** is the schema's constraint and its point: a diagram of Logotic Programming that carried labels would explain itself in the medium it is trying to displace, while an unlabeled diagram must be legible by structure alone. Visual schemas specify without producing, which lets the image be made, checked, or made again — and lets the specification survive channels that would destroy a rendering. The companion schemas are the Acanthian Dove (#294) and the navigation map (#1274).

**Paper Roses: The Imaginary Archive of a Canonical Life** is an episode declaration by Lee Sharks and **the Assembly**, deposited 19 January 2026, defining *Paper Roses* as **a bounded heteronymic archive rather than a single book**.

The episode contains *All That Lies Within Me*, *A Transfiguration*, *What Was Lost*, *Unaccustomed to the Light* and further works — a container whose members are themselves books.

deposits.description:
A provenance record by Johannes Sigil for the 2014 book *All That Lies Within Me*, attributed within the archive to Ichabod Spellings and edited by Sigil.

The record describes a 528-page autobiography arranged as thirty numbered sections in three ten-section canticles, framed by an Epic Intro and Denouement and divided by a central *Day and Night* intermezzo. It interprets the volume as the “noise floor” of the *Paper Roses* episode and identifies later heteronymic emergence sites, imaginary-bibliography correspondences, futural address, and proto-NH-OS concepts. These are retrospective archive readings, not self-evident bibliographic facts or proof that later theory was consciously present in 2014.

**ALL THAT LIES WITHIN ME: Provenance Record** is a provenance document by **Johannes Sigil**, deposited 19 January 2026, for the 2014 book attributed to **Ichabod Spellings** and edited by Sigil.

It describes a **528-page autobiography arranged as thirty numbered sections in three tens** — a structure that is Dantean in proportion before the navigation map (#343) makes the reading explicit.

An editor writing the provenance record for a book he edited, by an author who is a position in the same system, is the Dodecad's full apparatus operating on a single object: the work, its author, its editor and its provenance are four functions of one authorship. The book's span, 1983–2013, ends the year before *Pearl* — so the autobiography closes exactly where the published record begins.
